title: Federal Emergency Relief Programs Dashboards
before:
ESSER Federal Emergency Relief Funding Dashboard

The Federal Emergency Relief Funding Dashboard increases the visibility of the services being supported, facilitate public access to information about spending, and highlights the use of federal emergency funding at the local level. The Dashboard empowers all stakeholders – educators, families, and communities – to see allocations, reimbursements requested, and remaining funds.

American Rescue Plan School Operating Status Dashboard

As required by the US DOE, Maine asked each SAU to report the instructional model(s) being offered, attendance, and enrollment data for only APRIL 1, 2021. The dashboard shows data for mode of instruction, enrollment by mode of instruction for all students/race/ethnicity/other student groups, and attendance rate by mode of instruction for all students/other student groups.

decisions.label: Rebuild the heading outline
decisions.why: 2 headings sit at a level the page never opens — "ESSER Federal Emergency Relief Funding Dashboard" is an h3 with no h2 above it, so it is neither announced nor styled as the sub-section it is. Each heading moves to one level below whatever encloses it.

decisions.label: Turn the headings into section headers
decisions.why: 2 headings are plain text where every other page uses a section header, so the page reads as one continuous wall instead of parts.

decisions.why: It is the page’s own opening paragraph, moved into the banner rather than rewritten.

decisions.label: Size an image by its shape
decisions.why: "Dashboard with donut charts" measures 1185×787 — it was sitting in the flow at its own pixel size, aligned with nothing.

decisions.label: Size an image by its shape
decisions.why: "Dashboard with bar charts" measures 1069×827 — it was sitting in the flow at its own pixel size, aligned with nothing.

decisions.label: Stop a picture floating with nothing beside it
decisions.why: 2 pictures are set to float so text runs up beside them, but what follows them is a grid, a card or a table — a box, which clears the float rather than wrapping. So the picture sits alone with a column of white to its right and everything below starts past the bottom of it. Unfloated it is a picture in the flow, which is what it already looked like.
